newsitem.title: INDIA: Key supporter warns Indian PM over state alliance.
newsitem.headline: Key supporter warns Indian PM over state alliance.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Wednesday it could review its make-or-break support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority ruling alliance over a political row in populous Uttar Pradesh state.

Congress president Sitaram Kesri told a news conference his party wanted Deve Gowda's United Front to support a low-caste Hindu woman leader as Uttar Pradesh state chief minister after local polls there returned a hung assembly last week.
"Mayawati is not only a Dalit (lowest of Hindu castes) but also a woman. The Congress party is committed to make her the chief minister," Kesri said.
"We want (Deve Gowda's) government to remain in office, but if it continues to ignore our views, our high command will meet to take stock of our stand towards the government," Kesri said.

Kesri's remarks followed four days of wrangling between Mayawati's (one name) Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav's Samajwadi Party to form a state government in Uttar Pradesh.
The BSP fought the three-phase polls in alliance with Congress, but their combined tally was 100 seats in the 425-member assembly.
Yadav's Samajawdi Party, representing the main arm of the United Front in Uttar Pradesh, won 134 seats.
The standoff between Yadav and Mayawati prompted the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday to stake a claim to power in the state.
Uttar Pradesh, whose 140 million people make it more populous than Pakistan or Japan, is regarded as the main launching pad for the BJP's plans eventually to win power in New Delhi.
But the polls, which gave the BJP just 177 seats, were considered a major setback to India's main opposition party.
BJP officials told state governor Romesh Bhandari in the Uttar Pradesh capital Lucknow on Wednesday that they would have the required majority once their government was installed.
"The governor will be looking at all the aspects of the political equation before deciding the next move," an official in Lucknow told Reuters.

Uttar Pradesh was put under New Delhi's direct rule last year after Mayawati ditched an alliance with Yadav, then chief minister, to form her own government with BJP support. The alliance of convenience collapsed after a mere four months.
New Delhi's direct rule authority is due to expire on Thursday.
Deve Gowda came to power in June with the crucial support of 140 Congress deputies following inconclusive general elections.
He met Kesri on Tuesday and got him to address the United Front's decision-making Steering Committee over the Uttar Pradesh situation.
Front officials said there was no change in their support for Yadav's candidature after Kesri's appeal for Mayawati.
"The choice for the governor is to call the majority party or to extend direct rule in Uttar Pradesh," a United Front official told Reuters.
"If Mulayam Singh can muster more supporters than the BJP's tally, he should be invited to form the government," he said.
